indirect.label: Taxes on goods, services and trade

union.title: Union budget
union.total_label: Union receipts including the states' share of taxes
union.note: Receipts shown gross, before the states' share of taxes is passed on. Figures are Budget Estimates from Budget at a Glance 2026-27; some items marked 'rounded' come from its Budget Profile, which gives them in lakh crore to two decimals.

sources.title: Budget at a Glance 2026-27
sources.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Government of India

nodes.label: Companies
nodes.desc: Domestic and foreign companies taxed on their profits.

nodes.label: Individuals, families and firms
nodes.desc: Salaried people (tax deducted at source by employers, the closest India has to a payroll tax), the self-employed, Hindu undivided families, partnerships and investors (capital gains, securities transaction tax).

nodes.label: Buyers of goods and services
nodes.desc: GST is charged at each stage of supply, but businesses claim credit for GST they paid on inputs, so the tax ends up with the final buyer.

nodes.label: Buyers of fuel and tobacco
nodes.desc: Union excise now falls mostly on petrol, diesel and tobacco, which are outside GST or carry excise on top of it.

nodes.label: Importers
nodes.desc: Customs duty is paid by the importer and usually passed on in the price of imported goods and inputs.

nodes.label: Other taxpayers
nodes.desc: Smaller Union taxes and the taxes of Union territories without a legislature.

nodes.label: RBI and public-sector companies
nodes.desc: The Reserve Bank transfers its surplus (largely earnings on its foreign-currency and bond holdings), and public-sector companies pay dividends.

nodes.label: Fee payers, licensees and others
nodes.desc: Spectrum and other auction payments, licence fees, user charges, fines, receipts of Union territories and grants from foreign governments.

nodes.label: Borrowers repaying Union loans
nodes.desc: Mostly state governments and public enterprises paying interest on, and repaying, loans from the Union.

nodes.label: Buyers of government shares and assets
nodes.desc: Investors buying stakes in public-sector companies, and payments for leasing public assets (asset monetisation).

nodes.label: Bond buyers: banks, insurers, pension funds, foreign investors
nodes.desc: The Union borrows mainly by selling dated government securities, auctioned by the Reserve Bank on its behalf.

nodes.label: Small savers (PPF, post office, NSC)
nodes.desc: Deposits in small-savings schemes go to the National Small Savings Fund, which lends them to the Union.

nodes.label: Treasury bills, provident funds, external loans (net)
nodes.desc: Short-term treasury bills (₹1,30,000 crore), state provident funds (₹3,500 crore) and external debt (₹15,385 crore), less a net repayment of ₹45,801 crore of other internal debt and public-account liabilities.

nodes.label: The Union's own cash balance
nodes.desc: Drawing down cash held from earlier years.

nodes.label: Corporation tax
nodes.desc: Tax on company profits. Part of the pool shared with states.

nodes.label: Taxes on income
nodes.desc: Income tax on individuals, families and firms, including tax deducted from salaries and on capital gains.

nodes.label: Central GST
nodes.desc: The Union's half of GST on sales within a state, and its settled share of GST on sales between states. Rates are set by the GST Council. GST compensation cess, collected until 2025-26, is no longer budgeted.

nodes.label: Union excise duties
nodes.desc: Mostly on petrol, diesel and tobacco. Much of the duty on fuel is levied as a cess, which is not shared with states.

nodes.label: Customs
nodes.desc: Duties on imports, including cesses and surcharges on them.

nodes.label: Other taxes
nodes.desc: Other Union taxes (₹17,700 crore) and taxes of Union territories without a legislature (₹10,256 crore).

nodes.label: Fees, auctions and other non-tax
nodes.desc: Other non-tax revenue (₹2,29,373 crore), external grants (₹2,327 crore) and receipts of Union territories (₹1,765 crore).

nodes.label: Interest and loan repayments
nodes.desc: Interest received (₹41,763 crore) and recoveries of loans (₹38,397 crore).

nodes.label: Borrowing (the fiscal deficit)
nodes.desc: New borrowing needed to cover spending above receipts: ₹16,95,768 crore, 4.3% of GDP.

nodes.label: Union government
nodes.desc: Receipts go into the Consolidated Fund of India. Nothing can be spent from it without a law passed by Parliament (the Appropriation Act, Article 114); the Lok Sabha votes on each ministry's demand for grants, and the Comptroller and Auditor General audits the accounts.

nodes.label: States' share of Union taxes
nodes.desc: Part of the divisible pool of Union taxes (all taxes except cesses and surcharges) goes to states, in shares set by the Finance Commission. This is untied money; states decide how to spend it. 2026-27 is the first year under the 16th Finance Commission.

nodes.label: National Disaster Response Fund
nodes.desc: National Calamity Contingent Duty, collected on tobacco and some other goods, is passed to the disaster response fund.

nodes.label: State governments
nodes.desc: See the States diagram for how states raise and spend their money.

nodes.label: Disaster relief
nodes.desc: Released to states for relief after declared disasters.

links.note: Dated government securities (market borrowing).
Securities issued against small savings.

nodes.label: Interest
nodes.desc: Interest on the Union's debt.

nodes.label: Transport
nodes.desc: Highways (NHAI and road ministry), railways, civil aviation, shipping.

nodes.label: Defence
nodes.desc: Pay of the armed forces, operations and maintenance, and capital purchases (aircraft, ships, vehicles, equipment), much of it from public-sector and private manufacturers, domestic and foreign.

nodes.label: Pensions
nodes.desc: Pensions of retired Union government employees.

nodes.label: Rural development
nodes.desc: Rural employment guarantee, rural housing and roads; much of it is spent through states and panchayats.

nodes.label: Home affairs and Union territories
nodes.desc: Central armed police forces, intelligence, and the administration of Union territories.

nodes.label: Food subsidy
nodes.desc: Buying grain at minimum support prices and distributing it free or cheaply under the National Food Security Act.

nodes.label: Fertiliser subsidy
nodes.desc: Urea (₹1,16,805 crore) and nutrient-based subsidies (₹54,000 crore) paid to manufacturers and importers so farmers buy below cost.

nodes.label: Agriculture and allied
nodes.desc: Income support to farmers, crop insurance, interest subsidy on farm loans, and research.

nodes.label: Education
nodes.desc: School education grants to states and funding of central universities, IITs and other institutions.

nodes.label: Energy
nodes.desc: Power, renewable energy, petroleum and atomic energy programmes.

nodes.label: Health
nodes.desc: Health insurance for the poor, the National Health Mission (through states) and central hospitals.

nodes.label: Urban development
nodes.desc: Urban housing, metro rail, water and sanitation missions.

nodes.label: Commerce and industry
nodes.desc: Including production-linked incentives to manufacturers.

nodes.label: Tax administration
nodes.desc: Running the tax departments, and transfers to the GST compensation fund, which are being phased out.

nodes.label: Petroleum subsidy
nodes.desc: Mostly cooking-gas (LPG) support for poor households, paid through oil marketing companies.

nodes.label: Everything else
nodes.desc: All other ministries and items; includes ₹2 crore of rounding in the published table.

nodes.label: Bondholders and small savers
nodes.desc: Banks, insurers, provident and pension funds, the Reserve Bank, foreign investors and households who lent to the Union.

nodes.label: Food Corporation of India → ration-card holders
nodes.desc: The Food Corporation of India and state agencies buy grain from farmers and supply it through ration shops.

nodes.label: Government employees
nodes.desc: Salaries are spread across every purpose above; see 'By type' for the Union's salary bill.

nodes.label: Private firms on government contracts
nodes.desc: Amount not published as a single figure. Ministries and their agencies buy goods, works and services through open e-tenders on the Central Public Procurement Portal, the Government e-Marketplace (GeM), and for infrastructure through EPC contracts or public-private partnerships (build-operate-transfer, hybrid annuity, toll-operate-transfer). Contracts go to the qualifying bidder with the lowest price or best combined quality-and-cost score; firms are selected by the buying agency's tender committee, not elected.

sources.title: GeM records ₹18.4 trillion GMV since inception; MSMEs dominate FY26

nodes.fact: The Government e-Marketplace (GeM), used by Union and state bodies and public companies, handled orders worth about ₹5 lakh crore in 2025-26; 47% of that value went to micro and small enterprises.

nodes.label: Salaries
nodes.desc: Pay of Union civil employees counted as establishment expenditure (₹1.66 lakh crore in the Budget Profile, rounded). Pay of staff in autonomous bodies and some other units is counted under other heads.

nodes.label: Other running costs
nodes.desc: The rest of establishment expenditure: offices, travel, supplies and maintenance (₹3.62 lakh crore, rounded).

nodes.label: Grants to autonomous bodies
nodes.desc: IITs, AIIMS, central universities, research councils and regulators funded by grants (₹1.45 lakh crore, rounded).

nodes.label: Other central expenditure
nodes.desc: Other central-sector expenditure apart from interest and grants to autonomous bodies (₹2.12 lakh crore, rounded).

nodes.label: Union schemes and projects
nodes.desc: Central-sector schemes run by Union ministries and their agencies: highways, railways, defence purchases, the food and fertiliser subsidies, PM-KISAN and more.

nodes.label: Centrally sponsored schemes
nodes.desc: Schemes designed by the Union and run by states, usually with a state share: rural employment guarantee, Jal Jeevan Mission, Samagra Shiksha, National Health Mission and others.

nodes.label: Finance Commission grants
nodes.desc: Grants for urban local bodies (₹45,272 crore), rural local bodies (₹55,909 crore) and state disaster funds (₹28,216 crore).

nodes.label: Other transfers and loans to states
nodes.desc: Mainly 50-year interest-free loans to states for capital investment (₹1,85,000 crore), plus externally aided projects and other grants.

nodes.label: Private firms on government contracts
nodes.desc: Amount not published as a single figure. Ministries and their agencies buy goods, works and services through open e-tenders on the Central Public Procurement Portal, the Government e-Marketplace (GeM), and for infrastructure through EPC contracts or public-private partnerships (build-operate-transfer, hybrid annuity, toll-operate-transfer). Contracts go to the qualifying bidder with the lowest price or best combined quality-and-cost score; firms are selected by the buying agency's tender committee, not elected.

sources.title: GeM records ₹18.4 trillion GMV since inception; MSMEs dominate FY26

nodes.fact: The Government e-Marketplace (GeM), used by Union and state bodies and public companies, handled orders worth about ₹5 lakh crore in 2025-26; 47% of that value went to micro and small enterprises.

nodes.label: Subsidy and scheme beneficiaries
nodes.desc: Households and farmers receiving subsidised grain, fertiliser, cooking gas, cash transfers and other benefits, directly or through public and private intermediaries.

links.note: Includes ₹13,612 crore to Delhi and Puducherry; some goes to other implementing agencies.
Urban local bodies ₹45,272 crore; rural local bodies ₹55,909 crore.
State disaster response and mitigation funds.

states.title: All states combined
states.note: Shares of all states' combined revenue receipts. Receipts are 2025-26 budget estimates; own tax revenue (50%) is split using its 2025-26 composition. Spending shares are 2023-24 actuals (salaries and pensions 39%, interest about 14%, subsidies 9%). States also borrow, which is not shown. Per-state figures are on the roadmap.

nodes.label: Vehicle owners, electricity users, landholders, professionals
State GST
nodes.desc: 44% of states' own tax revenue.

nodes.label: Sales tax / VAT on fuel and alcohol
nodes.desc: 20% of own tax revenue. Petroleum products and alcohol for drinking are outside GST.

nodes.label: State excise on alcohol
nodes.desc: 14% of own tax revenue. Close to nothing in states with prohibition, such as Bihar and Gujarat.

nodes.label: Stamp duty and registration
nodes.desc: 12% of own tax revenue.

nodes.label: Other state taxes
nodes.desc: The remaining 10% of own tax revenue: vehicle tax, electricity duty, land revenue, professional tax and others.

nodes.label: Own non-tax revenue
nodes.desc: Mining royalties and auction premiums, forest revenue, liquor licence fees, lotteries, user charges and dividends from state companies. Higher in mineral-rich states.

nodes.label: Grants from the Union
nodes.desc: Centrally sponsored scheme funds and Finance Commission grants.

nodes.label: State governments (all states)
nodes.desc: Each state's receipts go into its own Consolidated Fund; the Legislative Assembly must pass an Appropriation Act before money is spent (Article 204). States also borrow, about 3.3% of GDP in 2025-26, which is not shown here.

nodes.label: Salaries and pensions
nodes.desc: Teachers, police, health workers, revenue staff and others, and retired employees.

nodes.label: Subsidies
nodes.desc: Largely power subsidies to farmers and households, paid to electricity distribution companies, plus food and transport subsidies.

nodes.label: Everything else
nodes.desc: Schemes, cash transfers, grants to local bodies, operations and maintenance. States spent more than their revenue receipts in 2023-24; the gap was borrowed.

nodes.label: Holders of state bonds
nodes.desc: State development loans are bought mostly by banks, insurers and provident funds.

nodes.label: Private firms on government contracts
nodes.desc: Amount not published as a single figure. Ministries and their agencies buy goods, works and services through open e-tenders on the state e-procurement portals, the Government e-Marketplace (GeM), and for infrastructure through EPC contracts or public-private partnerships (build-operate-transfer, hybrid annuity, toll-operate-transfer). Contracts go to the qualifying bidder with the lowest price or best combined quality-and-cost score; firms are selected by the buying agency's tender committee, not elected.

local.title: Panchayats and municipalities
local.note: Who pays local bodies and what they pay for. There is no reliable, current all-India total for local body finances yet, so this diagram shows the routes without sizes. The Finance Commission grant is the one national figure.
